pr.title: Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins

raw_findings.body: The row remains a normal-flow container, so the panel is not a flex item; its new auto margin and order declarations do not provide the intended right alignment or ordering, and the header controls can flow or wrap incorrectly.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Header layout rules intended for flex items are ignored and the controls fall back to ordinary block/float layout.
raw_findings.impact: The row remains a normal-flow container, so the panel is not a flex item; its new auto margin and order declarations do not provide the intended right alignment or ordering, and the header controls can flow or wrap incorrectly.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch enables flex layout on an ancestor whose only direct child is the non-flex `.row`, rather than on the element containing the header layout siblings.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Apply the flexbox mixin to `.row` (or remove the extra wrapper) so that `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper`, and `.panel` are direct flex items before relying on `margin-left: auto` and `order`.
raw_findings.title: Apply the flex container to the header row that owns the controls
raw_findings.trigger: Render the header using the supplied markup, where `.contents` contains a `.row` and the `.title` and `.panel` elements are nested inside that row.

raw_findings.body: The prefixed flex container renders, but cross-axis centering or baseline alignment is ignored, leaving header and small-action contents vertically misaligned.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The browser falls back to its default cross-axis alignment despite the caller requesting `center` or `baseline`.
raw_findings.impact: The prefixed flex container renders, but cross-axis centering or baseline alignment is ignored, leaving header and small-action contents vertically misaligned.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mixin adds a Mozilla legacy flex display declaration but omits the corresponding Mozilla legacy alignment property.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Emit `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside the existing legacy display fallback, or remove the obsolete Mozilla display fallback and explicitly limit the supported browser range.
raw_findings.title: Add the legacy Firefox alignment fallback to the flexbox mixin
raw_findings.trigger: Use the new mixin in a Firefox version that supports the prefixed `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box` display syntax but does not support unprefixed `align-items`.

raw_findings.body: The panel no longer has the previous right-float fallback; `margin-left: auto` has no equivalent effect on the normal-flow block, so login or header controls can lose their right-aligned placement.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unsupported browsers lay out the header panel in normal flow instead of maintaining the established right-aligned header layout.
raw_findings.impact: The panel no longer has the previous right-float fallback; `margin-left: auto` has no equivalent effect on the normal-flow block, so login or header controls can lose their right-aligned placement.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch removes the only legacy positioning rule while introducing flexbox without a non-flex fallback path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep `float: right` as the non-flex fallback and override it only when the panel is a child of a supported flex container, or provide an equivalent feature-gated fallback.
raw_findings.title: Retain a non-flex fallback for the header panel float
raw_findings.trigger: Render the header in a browser that supports none of the emitted flexbox display declarations, such as an older browser without flexbox support.

finding.trigger: Render the header using the supplied markup, where `.contents` contains a `.row` and the `.title` and `.panel` elements are nested inside that row.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that `.contents` containing a `.row` wrapper makes `.panel` not a flex item is based on assumed HTML structure. The actual HTML in `_header.html.erb` shows `.contents > .row > .title/.panel`, but the patch applies flexbox to `.contents`. The candidate assumes `.row` blocks flex behavior, but the patch context shows `.panel` rules with `margin-left: auto` and `order` are defined directly under `.d-header`, not requiring `.panel` to be a direct child of `.contents`. The claim about incorrect flex container target is speculative without proof the current markup breaks.

finding.trigger: Use the new mixin in a Firefox version that supports the prefixed `-moz-box`/`-moz-inline-box` display syntax but does not support unprefixed `align-items`.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that `-moz-box-align` is missing is technically accurate, but the trigger requires Firefox versions supporting `-moz-box` but not unprefixed `align-items`. Such Firefox versions (pre-22) are extremely old (2013) and not realistically supported. The `flexbox()` mixin includes `-moz-box` display, but browsers requiring that prefix are obsolete. The impact is not realistic for any supported browser range.

finding.title: Retain a non-flex fallback for the header panel float
finding.trigger: Render the header in a browser that supports none of the emitted flexbox display declarations, such as an older browser without flexbox support.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch does remove `float: right` from `.panel` (visible at L37 on LEFT side), but the claim that browsers without flexbox support will break is unrealistic. The flexbox mixin emits multiple vendor prefixes covering IE10+, Safari 6+, and all modern browsers. Browsers truly lacking all flexbox support are obsolete (IE9 and earlier). The trigger scenario of 'a browser that supports none of the emitted flexbox display declarations' is not a realistic concern for any supported browser.
